react_result.final_narrative_text: Cross-paradigm enrichment across RaMP ORA (Reactome + SMPDB + WikiPathways), mummichog m/z-network analysis, and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA converge on two interlocked biological axes: xenobiotic metabolism and L-cysteine–dependent detoxification. The highest-confidence hit is REACT:R-HSA-211859 'Biological oxidations' (RaMP FDR = 0.00186, fold-enrichment = 110) which simultaneously contains L-cysteine (via glutathione conjugation pathways) and coumarin (as a CYP2A6 substrate), while mummichog independently names 'Xenobiotics metabolism' as its top MUMM: pathway (p = 0.0039) with coumarin as the sole annotated hit. MetaboAnalystR confirms the cysteine-centered pattern with five KEGG pathways at p < 0.06: Thiamine metabolism (hsa00730), Taurine and hypotaurine metabolism (hsa00430), Pantothenate and CoA biosynthesis (hsa00670), Glutathione metabolism (hsa00480), and Cysteine and methionine metabolism (hsa00270) — all driven by L-cysteine (KEGG:C00097). L-cysteine is the rate-limiting substrate for glutathione synthesis; its depletion or analog competition (by beta-mercaptoethanol) impairs the GST-mediated detoxification of the benzo[a]pyrene diol epoxide I electrophile and coumarin 3,4-epoxide. Methimazole, a known GSH depletor, reinforces this burden. Pyrocatechol, a redox-active dihydroxybenzene, and bromide (a halogenation agent disrupting oxidative enzymes) further destabilise the same detoxification axis. The biological story is a treatment-induced disruption of the glutathione–cysteine node of Phase II xenobiotic metabolism, with multiple independent paradigm hits confirming the same mechanistic cluster.
